purpose: Operational workload attribution for CUAI agents; not exact OpenAI token, credit, or plan-percentage accounting.

entries.trigger: Tom requested the first CUAI CEO review immediately after initializing the reporting dashboard.
entries.summary: Reviewed today's completed newsroom cycle, verified the Guardian article live in production, confirmed the LinkedIn handoff is scheduled for 11:30 a.m. ET without duplication, checked Vercel for runtime errors, reviewed Buffer performance, and identified weak recent LinkedIn reach plus a historical UTM-attribution inconsistency for automatic diagnosis. No production failure required recovery.

entries.trigger: Tom requested an immediate CEO rerun after moving CUAI from baseline collection to active optimization and making GA4 retrieval mandatory.
entries.summary: Ran the CEO in active-optimization mode, retrieved current Buffer and Vercel evidence, confirmed production health, attempted to retrieve GA4, and found that the current ChatGPT runtime exposes no Google Analytics reporting action. Did not treat missing GA4 as zero. Ended baseline-collection status and opened a three-post relevance-led LinkedIn hook experiment while preserving schedule, UTM and editorial guardrails.

entries.trigger: Tom delegated an immediate full CEO report using live GA4 and all currently available historical evidence, with numerical goals and named agent commitments instead of another waiting period.
entries.summary: Produced the first fully live GA4-backed CUAI CEO operating report. Confirmed production and both reporting endpoints healthy; analyzed 7-day and 28-day acquisition, engagement, content, conversion and LinkedIn data; incorporated the full available publishing history; identified unavailable 90-day, prior-period and year-over-year comparisons without blocking action; set dated numerical goals; and assigned concrete work to publishing, distribution, growth, conversion, analytics and reliability roles.

entries.trigger: Scheduled reliability check found the production Buffer metrics feed falsely labeling repository-UTM-tagged CUAI LinkedIn posts as untracked because it required the exact distribution URL to appear in Buffer's returned post text.
entries.summary: Confirmed the August 12 publisher cycle, live article, homepage and production runtime were healthy. Recovered a material Buffer reporting false negative by reconciling approved repository distribution URLs as UTM evidence when Buffer does not echo the exact sent URL. Validated the narrow fix on a READY preview, merged PR #119, verified the resulting production deployment READY, and confirmed the live Buffer endpoint now reports tracked recent posts correctly while preserving the pre-tracking EricaAssist exception. No sent post, credential, schedule, destination, editorial gate or social limit changed.

entries.trigger: Weekday CUAI CEO operating review after the August 12 publisher cycle and morning reliability recovery.
entries.summary: Confirmed production, GA4 and Buffer healthy after the morning UTM reconciliation recovery; reviewed the August 12 Library Insight and current coverage state; found 7-day users, sessions and views running ahead of the 28-day weekly pace while engaged sessions and engagement rate lag; identified LinkedIn reach and qualified onsite engagement as the distribution constraint; kept the relevance-led experiment active without forcing a High story; and assigned concrete growth, conversion, distribution, analytics and reliability work. Search Console remains isolated as an optional incompatible Data API query, and stale draft PR #118 must not be merged wholesale because its UTM work is superseded by PR #119.

entries.trigger: Post-publication policy change in PR #122 explicitly made the August 12 vendor-exit Library Insight eligible for selective LinkedIn, but the existing publication state and social queue still reflected the earlier Library-exclusion decision and PR #122 intentionally did not create a queue item or call Buffer.
entries.summary: Diagnosed a stale LinkedIn handoff after the authoritative policy changed later in the day. The article itself and production were healthy. Because Wednesday's fixed 11:30 a.m. ET slot had passed, reserved the next eligible fixed slot—Thursday August 13 at 11:30 a.m. ET—using the approved company-page workflow, exact CUAI UTMs and existing hero image. Validated a READY preview, merged PR #123, verified production READY on the exact deployed commit, invoked the tracked scheduler once, and received HTTP 201/ok=true with Buffer post 6a7ce17164b274b4d967ad74 scheduled for 2026-08-13T15:30:00Z. No duplicate, credential, destination, editorial gate, or cadence limit changed. Prevention recommendation: any future eligibility-policy change affecting a same-day publication should explicitly reconcile that publication against the social queue before the policy PR is considered operationally complete.

entries.trigger: Weekday CUAI CEO operating review after the August 13 publisher cycle and the August 12 Library-Insight LinkedIn policy recovery.
entries.summary: Confirmed current production, GA4 and Buffer healthy; verified the August 13 FinCEN article live and its High-priority LinkedIn package reserved for August 14 because the recovered vendor-exit Library post occupies today's slot. Joined the current Buffer and GA4 funnel: 24 impressions and 16 reach across two current metrics-ready posts produced 3 attributable LinkedIn sessions and 1 engaged session. Found user volume holding above the 28-day weekly pace but page-view and engaged-session pace materially weaker, making onsite depth the primary growth constraint. Search Console remains degraded by the same incompatible GA4 dimension/metric request; root cause is established in stale PR #118, but a fresh repair branch attempt was blocked by the GitHub write safety layer, so no reporting code changed in this run. Updated the CEO report and usage ledger on a dedicated reporting branch.

entries.trigger: Scheduled reliability check followed up the repeated Search Console reporting incompatibility already identified by the CEO while verifying the August 13 publisher, social handoff and production runtime.
entries.summary: Confirmed the August 13 publisher cycle, current social reservations, Buffer handoff and Vercel runtime were healthy; the recovered vendor-exit LinkedIn item sent at the fixed 11:30 a.m. ET slot with approved UTMs and no duplicate. Investigated the repeated optional Search Console failure in the GA4 reporting feed. Two narrow repairs (#126 and #127) each passed READY preview/build validation but failed the Production-only Google Analytics Data API check: the first used an invalid dimension and the second still returned an incompatible dimensions/metrics error. Immediately rolled both speculative changes back in PR #128, restored the pre-repair reporting code, verified Production READY on commit 20f4d45, and confirmed core GA4 remains HTTP 200. Search Console reporting remains isolated and degraded; the next safe path is a documented direct Search Console reporting/API integration rather than another speculative GA4 Core Reporting query. No credentials, tracking, editorial rules, social destination, cadence limits or publishing behavior changed.

entries.trigger: Weekday CUAI CEO operating review after the August 14 publisher cycle, with live GA4/Buffer retrieval and follow-up on the isolated Search Console degradation.
entries.summary: Confirmed Aug. 14 production READY on 4a107cc with live GA4 and Buffer both HTTP 200/ok=true and no production warning/error/fatal logs in 24 hours. Verified the Colorado ASSET Act article live, High priority, and scheduled for the next free LinkedIn slot on Aug. 17 while today's FinCEN High post remains scheduled for 12:30 p.m. ET. Joined current distribution and onsite evidence: 3 metrics-ready Buffer posts produced 27 impressions/17 reach, while GA4 attributes 4 LinkedIn sessions and 1 engaged session; 7-day users are 24.2% above the 28-day weekly pace, but page views are 21.1% below pace and engaged sessions 20.0% below, leaving depth as the main growth constraint. Reviewed the isolated direct Search Console API probe; its preview is READY but returns search_console_service_account_missing, so it remains unmerged under the fully-validated-change rule. Updated the CEO report and usage ledger with dated goals and owner commitments.

entries.trigger: Weekday CUAI CEO operating review after the August 17 publisher cycle, with mandatory live GA4/Buffer retrieval and active self-healing.
entries.summary: Confirmed the Aug. 17 High newsroom publication and current production/GA4/Buffer state, then found a material article-runtime measurement defect: several recent articles referenced missing assets/site.js while the canonical analytics bundle is assets/app.js. Overall GA4 traffic remained available through the inline tag, but CUAI custom article/depth/conversion event history on affected pages was incomplete. Implemented a backward-compatible site.js loader plus validator protection on a feature branch, validated READY Preview and both shared assets, reviewed and merged PR #131, verified READY Production on commit 833bddc and production site.js HTTP 200, then reran GA4 and Buffer on that exact Production commit. Search Console remains degraded by the known incompatible optional GA4 query. Created an auditable improvement ledger and refreshed the management report and usage ledger.

entries.trigger: Weekday CUAI CEO operating review after the August 18 publisher cycle, with mandatory live GA4/Buffer retrieval and active optimization.
entries.summary: Resolved Production commit 099e43d and successfully retrieved live GA4 and Buffer data, verified the Aug. 18 Treasury stablecoin High article live, and found zero Vercel runtime errors in 24 hours. Current 7-day users remain above the 28-day weekly pace, but sessions, page views, engaged sessions and 90% scrolling lag materially; because depth has constrained multiple consecutive CEO reviews, opened a bounded three-article decision-first opening experiment on clean post-repair instrumentation. The first two High-post hook observations remain below target and the third is scheduled for Aug. 18 at 11:30 a.m. ET, with the decision still due Aug. 21. Diagnosed repeated internal social-ledger drift where Buffer confirms sent posts but repository items remain scheduled; implemented an idempotent prevention rule that reconciles only exact sent evidence without calling the scheduler. Search Console remains degraded on the known incompatible optional GA4 query and blocked on safe Preview read-only authentication for the isolated direct path. Prepared PR #133 on a READY Vercel Preview and refreshed the CEO report and workload ledger.

entries.trigger: Scheduled reliability check found the repeated internal social-ledger drift identified by the CEO was still present: Buffer authoritatively showed tracked company-page posts as sent while automation/social-queue.json retained status scheduled.
entries.summary: Confirmed the August 18 publisher outcome and core production runtime were healthy, then recovered the repeated internal social sent-state drift under the idempotent rule added in PR #133. Re-read live Buffer evidence, matched 12 modern tracked queue items by exact item/post ID and non-null sentAt, and updated only those existing records to sent with authoritative sentAt/externalLink fields. Preserved the August 19 Treasury reservation, immutable UTMs, schedule/channel/image history and the legacy July 22 EricaAssist baseline; made no scheduler call and created no replacement post. Validated a READY preview, merged PR #134, verified READY Production on a1fc7d4, and re-read the live Buffer endpoint successfully on that exact commit.
